search.what: Filters the list below by network name, address range (CIDR) or interface name (wg0, wg1…).
search.who: Anyone looking for one network among many.
search.effect: Only changes what this page shows; nothing is saved or changed on the server.

name.what: The name of the new VPN network, shown in the network selector, the topology and the firewall rules.
name.who: Operators who keep separate networks for groups of devices (for example office, servers, staff).
name.effect: Must be unique. It cannot be renamed later: to change it, delete the network and create it again.

cidr.what: The network’s address range, a /24 inside the address pool (Settings). Empty: the server picks the next free one. The hub takes the first address; devices start from the third.
cidr.who: Every network needs one: it decides which addresses its devices use.
cidr.effect: It may not overlap another network and cannot be changed later. Device configs route the whole pool, so a new network inside it needs no new config on any device. A new WireGuard interface (wg1, wg2…) is created on the first free UDP port after wg0’s 51820; that port must be reachable from the internet.

clientDns.what: The DNS servers this network’s devices resolve names with: up to 3 IPv4 addresses, comma-separated. Device configs name the hub’s address in this network (for example 10.10.0.1) as DNS; the hub forwards the queries to the servers here.
clientDns.who: Networks whose devices must resolve names with a particular server (for example an internal DNS reached over the VPN).
clientDns.effect: Empty: full-tunnel devices use 1.1.1.1 (through the hub), split-tunnel devices keep their own DNS. Changing the servers changes no device config — the hub forwards to the new ones at once. Only going from empty to set or back (a split-tunnel config gaining or losing its DNS line) makes configs outdated once.

tunnelMode.what: What this network’s devices send through the server: VPN (split) sends only traffic to the VPN networks; full tunnel sends all internet traffic, so the server is their way to the internet.
tunnelMode.who: Split suits most networks. Full tunnel suits devices that must browse through the server, e.g. on public Wi-Fi or to appear with the server’s IP address.
tunnelMode.effect: It applies to every device of the network that has no own mode. Devices only switch after their config is downloaded again. Full tunnel raises the server’s traffic; it needs an admin, and on the Admin VPN the nftables engine.

owner.what: The user who owns this network. Whoever creates a network becomes its owner.
owner.who: Admins moving a network to a user whose role shows only their own networks, or taking it back.
owner.effect: The new owner sees and manages the network at once (its devices and configs too); the previous owner no longer sees it, if their role shows only their own networks. Other roles are not affected.
